title: Tuki 1736 (Missale Copto-Arabicum): Bohairic Coptic St. Basil Anaphora core constituent — independent pixel-collation review
scope: Complete Bohairic Coptic column of the St. Basil Anaphora core in Raphael Tuki's 1736 Rome Missale Copto-Arabicum (ULB Bonn digital copy, Part II printed pp. 96-116 / PDF pp. 389-409): from the Anaphora heading ⲦⲀⲚⲀⲪⲞⲢⲀ ⲛ̀ⲧⲉ ⲡⲓⲁ̀ⲅⲓⲟⲥ ⲂⲀⲤⲒⲖⲒⲞⲤ ⲙ̀ Ⲫⲓⲱⲧ and Opening Dialogue on II.96 (PDF p. 389), through Preface, printed Pre-Sanctus hymns, Sanctus, Post-Sanctus, Institution Narrative of Bread and Cup (including Ⲁϥϫⲉⲙϯⲡⲓ 'He tasted' at II.110 / PDF p. 403), Anamnesis, and Epiclesis (including Tuki's printed Ⲡⲭ̅ⲥ̅ at II.114 / PDF p. 407) through the concluding communion-fruits petition Ⲁⲣⲓⲧⲉⲛ ⲛⲉⲙⲡ̀ϣⲁ ⲧⲏⲣⲉⲛ ... ⲓⲥϫⲉⲛ ⲡⲉⲛⲉϩ. on II.116 (PDF p. 409) immediately before the Great Intercessions (Ⲁⲣⲓⲫⲙⲉⲩⲓ̀ Ⲡϭ̅ⲥ̅...). Excludes the parallel Arabic translation column, Arabic-only rubrics, running heads, page numerals, catchwords, and later blue/purple manuscript reader annotations.
method: Independent pixel-level visual inspection of all rendered facsimile pages by independent-collator-v3-alex-west (distinct from drafter AI source transcriber (Lane T3, direct PNG inspection of Tuki 1736 PDF pp. 389-409)) on 2026-11-25. Applied 57 pixel-verified correction(s) relative to initial draft; verified every unit boundary, page account (1..676), and SHA-256 hash.
normalization_limit: Direct reading from 200-dpi rendered PNG images of Tuki 1736 PDF pp. 389-409 (Part II pp. 96-116). UTF-8 NFC, LTR, LF line endings. All Coptic-column letters—including Greek liturgical acclamations set in Tuki's single Bohairic Coptic typeface—are encoded strictly in Unicode Coptic (U+2C80-U+2CFF) and the seven Demotic-derived Coptic letters in Greek-and-Coptic (U+03E2-U+03EF: Ϣ/ϣ, Ϥ/ϥ, Ϧ/ϧ, Ϩ/ϩ, Ϫ/ϫ, Ϭ/ϭ, Ϯ/ϯ), with zero non-Coptic Greek-block letters (U+0370-U+03E1). Bohairic jinkim/syllabic grave marks are encoded as combining grave accent (U+0300); nomina sacra/abbreviation bars (Ⲡϭ̅ⲥ̅, Ⲓⲏ̅ⲥ̅, Ⲡⲭ̅ⲥ̅, Ⲡⲛ̅ⲁ̅, ⲉⲑ̅ⲩ̅, Ⲕⲉ̅, Ⲑ̅ⲥ̅, ⲁ̀ⲗ̅) as combining overline (U+0305); printed red 8-pointed cross-rosettes marking signs of the cross as ✠ (U+2720). Tuki's line-end double-slash word-wrap hyphens ('//') are joined across lines; page-foot catchwords, running heads, Coptic page numerals and Arabic column/rubrics are excluded. Printed punctuation normalized as ':' (colon), '·' (U+00B7, Tuki's raised s-shaped/single stop), and '.' (full stop). Tuki's printed readings are preserved verbatim without silent emendation (including ⲫⲓⲙ and ⲉ̀ⲧⲟ̀ϩⲓⲉ̀ⲣⲁⲧⲟⲩ p. 391, ⲡⲉⲛⲉⲩⲙⲁⲧⲓ p. 392, ⲛ̀ⲑⲉⲕ, ⲉⲑⲛⲉⲥⲟⲥ, ϯⲑⲉⲟ̀ⲧⲩⲕⲟⲥ, ⲡⲓⲁ̀ⲙⲟϩⲓ, and ⲙ̀ⲙⲁⲓⲣⲡⲙⲓ p. 394, ⲩⲫⲱⲣϣ, ⲁⲩⲧⲩⲛ, and ⲧⲩⲛ p. 395, ⲟⲩⲙⲟⲛⲉ̀ⲃⲟⲗ p. 397, letterpress ⲉ̀ⲃⲟⲗϧⲛ p. 402 excluding later purple superscript ⲉ, Ⲁϥϫⲉⲙϯⲡⲓ p. 403, Ⲡⲭ̅ⲥ̅ in Epiclesis p. 407, and Ⲡⲣⲩⲥⲭⲱⲙⲉⲛ p. 407).
review_limit: Complete declared constituent only, not whole-book transcription or diplomatic typography.
